aliases: 10.7554/eLife.105343.2 (journal version cited by the code repository README; NOT the version assessed here)

reproduction_target: Evaluation of first-, second- and third-generation DNA methylation clocks in 621 Alzheimer's disease cases and non-demented controls from the MAGENTA study (white, African American, Puerto Rican, Cuban and Peruvian cohorts). Computational target: Illumina Infinium Global Screening Array genotype QC, FLARE local-ancestry inference against 1000 Genomes CEU / PEL / YRI reference panels and derivation of global ancestry proportions, openSeSAMe (SeSAMe) probe filtering and Noob normalisation of Illumina HumanMethylation EPICv2.0 methylation arrays, epigenetic age estimation with the methylClock R library for the Horvath, Hannum, Zhang2019 EN, Zhang2019 BLUP and PhenoAge clocks plus a separately applied DunedinPACE clock, impute.knn imputation of missing clock CpGs, Pearson correlation of DNAm age against chronological age with between-cohort correlation comparison via cocor (Fisher z test, Zou confidence intervals), raw / intrinsic / extrinsic age-acceleration estimation with Mann-Whitney U testing of AD cases versus controls, a mean-of-five-clocks ensemble predictor, differential methylation between 306 African-ancestry and 300 European-ancestry EWAS Hub whole-blood samples by linear regression with sex and age covariates at Benjamini-Hochberg FDR < 0.05, bedtools intersection of clock CpGs with gnomAD v3.0 variants in hg38, assembly of three published blood meQTL sets (Hawe 2022, Shang 2023, Villicana 2023 / EPIGEN) filtered at BH FDR 0.05 and lifted hg19 -> hg38 with UCSC liftOver, intersection of meQTL target CpGs with each clock's CpG set, and allele-frequency analysis of the resulting 29,033 clock meQTL tag variants across ten gnomAD v4.1 global population groups and across African / Amerindigenous / European local-ancestry blocks in 7,612 gnomAD v3.1 Latino admixed individuals.
granularity_note: One step per named tool or named analysis invocation in the Methods section of the bioRxiv v2 full text (JATS XML retrieved by direct HTTP GET on 2026-07-28 after WebFetch returned HTTP 403; title string 'Methylation Clocks Do Not Predict Age' verified present in the fetched XML before scoring), following guide Step 1 coarse granularity. Sample ascertainment, genotyping array hybridisation and methylation array hybridisation are lumped into 3 W steps and are out of computational-reproduction scope. The code repository landing page and README prose were read (README.md 117 lines, retrieved raw from the main branch), including the declared directory listing (environment.yml, data/, scripts/01..11_*.R, manuscript/) and the conda installation and step-by-step replication instructions. environment.yml (27 lines) was opened because the capture_claim field turns on whether the declared conda environment constrains versions; no analysis script was read, which is stage-2 work. IMPORTANT VERSION-OF-RECORD NOTE: the repository README describes the later journal version of this work ('Methylation Clocks Fail to Generalize Across Genetically Admixed Individuals', eLife 10.7554/eLife.105343.2) with replication cohorts (GENOA, Grady Trauma Project, Swedish), principal-component clocks and a six-figure layout that do not appear in the assessed bioRxiv v2 preprint. Steps were enumerated from the preprint Methods, and repository code coverage was credited only where a named script plausibly implements the preprint step.

steps.label: Wet-lab / clinical: MAGENTA cohort ascertainment at five sites (University of Miami Miller School of Medicine, Wake Forest University, Case Western Reserve University, Universidad Central Del Caribe, Instituto Nacional de Ciencias Neurologicas), consistent ascertainment protocols capturing cognitive function, family history, sociodemographic factors and dementia staging, AD diagnoses assigned by clinical experts under NIA-AA criteria, blood sample collection under site-specific IRB-approved protocols with written informed consent.
Wet-lab: genome-wide SNP genotyping on the Illumina Infinium Global Screening Array, described as 'previously performed as previously described for the MAGENTA study cohorts'.

Wet-lab: DNA methylation quantification on the Illumina HumanMethylation EPICv2.0 array 'according to the manufacturer's instructions' (bisulfite conversion; GCT score used downstream as a conversion-completeness metric).

Genotype quality control: 'standard quality control filters on call rate, quality, missingness, and Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium' applied to the Illumina Infinium Global Screening Array data. No tool named, no thresholds given, deferred to prior MAGENTA publications.

Local ancestry inference with the FLARE software (S. R. Browning, Waples, and B. L. Browning, 2023) using three 1000 Genomes Project reference panels: CEU (Utah residents with Northern and Western European ancestry), PEL (Peruvians in Lima) and YRI (Yoruba in Ibadan, Nigeria).

Global ancestry proportion estimation: 'we summed the haplotype lengths for each ancestry in each individual and divided by the total number of sites considered', producing per-individual African / European / American proportions used to stratify every downstream comparison.

Methylation array QC and normalisation with the openSeSAMe pipeline from the SeSAMe tools (Wanding Zhou, 2018): removal of poorly designed probes, removal of probes with signal detection P-value > 0.05 in more than 5% of samples, removal of non-CG probes and probes on chromosomes X, Y and MT, exclusion of samples with incomplete bisulfite conversion (GCT score > 1.5) and of principal-component-analysis outliers, then Noob normalisation with nonlinear dye-bias correction.

Epigenetic age estimation with 'established implementations of the Horvath, Hannum, Zhang2019 EN, Zhang2019 BLUP, and PhenoAge clocks from the methylClock R library (Pelegi-Siso et al., 2021)'; 'Unless otherwise specified, default options were used for all clocks'; clock CpG sets 'taken from the methylclock library or the original publication'.

DunedinPACE third-generation pace-of-aging clock applied separately 'because it was not included in the methyl-clock library' (Belsky et al., 2022). Excluded from the age-correlation analyses because it does not predict age; used for the AD case/control pace comparison.

Imputation of missing clock CpG methylation: 'the methylClock library imputes methylation status using the mpute.knn [impute.knn] function from the impute R library'. Reported missingness 3.7% (Horvath), 12.7% (Hannum), 4.5% (Zhang2019 EN), 3.7% (PhenoAge), 17.9% (DunedinPACE).
Pearson correlation of estimated epigenetic age with chronological age computed for the control individuals in each MAGENTA cohort (white, African American, Puerto Rican, Cuban, Peruvian).

Between-cohort comparison of correlation strength: 'we computed p-values for the observed differences using Fisher's z test and the Zou method for computing confidence intervals as implemented in the cocor library (Diedenhofen and Musch, 2015)'.

Epigenetic age acceleration estimation: 'we estimated raw, intrinsic, and extrinsic age acceleration for all clocks, except DunedinPACE, from the methylClock library'; intrinsic age acceleration (independent of blood cell proportions) reported in the main text.

Case/control comparison of age acceleration: 'we compared epigenetic age association between AD cases and matched controls using a Mann-Whitney U test, as implemented in the stats library in R. We analyzed the study as a whole and stratified by cohort.'

Ensemble age predictor: 'The ensemble was computed as the average of the estimate of each method on each individual' over the Horvath, Hannum, Zhang2019 EN, Zhang2019 BLUP and PhenoAge clocks, then re-evaluated for age-prediction accuracy and for ensemble intrinsic age acceleration against AD status.

Differential methylation between genetic ancestries: 'we analyzed whole blood methylation data from the EWAS Hub for 306 individuals of African (AFR) and 300 of European (EUR) ancestry. We fitted a linear regression model to the whole blood methylation profiles for these two sets of individuals, including covariates for sex and chronological age. We called differentially methylated CpG sites in AFR vs. EUR individuals with a multiple testing adjusted p-value < 0.05 (Benjamini-Hochberg FDR correction)', then intersected the differentially methylated sites with the Horvath, Hannum, Zhang2019 EN, PhenoAge and DunedinPACE clock CpGs.

Analysis of genetic variation at clock CpG sites: 'we intersected all the clock CpGs with variants identified in version 3.0 of gnomAD (Karczewski et al., 2020)' covering 76,156 whole-genome-sequenced individuals; 'The intersection was performed using bedtools in hg38 coordinates (Quinlan and Hall, 2010)'. Yields the 245/353 disrupted-Horvath-CpG result and the allele-frequency distribution of Figure 4.

meQTL set assembly from three published blood studies: 11,165,559 meQTLs from 3,799 Europeans and 3,195 South Asians (Hawe et al., 2022), 4,565,687 meQTLs from 961 African Americans (Shang et al., 2023), and 249,710 meQTLs from 2,358 UK individuals (Villicana et al., 2023, EPIGEN); 'We filtered these sets separately on at a false discovery rate threshold of 0.05, correcting for multiple tests using the Benjamini-Hochberg method.'

Coordinate conversion: 'These meQTL studies published their results in hg19 coordinates. To integrate with genetic variation and clock CpG data, we mapped the meQTL positions to hg38 using the UCSC liftOver tool (Hinrichs, 2006).' No chain file identified, no unmapped-record policy stated.

meQTL-to-clock intersection: 'For each meQTL set, we intersected the target CpG site with the CpGs considered in each clock and then combined across meQTL sets to generate a set of clock CpGs with evidence of meQTL.' Produces the headline counts (271/353 Horvath CpGs with at least one meQTL, 29,033 unique variants) and the per-clock proportions of Figure 6 (Hannum 8%, Zhang2019 EN 1%, PhenoAge 7%, DunedinPACE 0%).

Global-population allele frequencies of clock meQTL: 'We used version 4.1 to quantify the allele frequencies of these meQTLs in the following global populations: African, Middle Eastern, Admixed American, European (non-Finnish), South Asian, Ashkenazi Jewish, East Asian, European (Finnish), Amish, and a Remaining group', with the reported comparison of median African frequency 0.068 against 0.004-0.046 in the other eight groups at p < 3.85e-25. The statistical test producing that p-value is not named in the Methods.

Local-ancestry allele frequencies of clock meQTL: 'We then used gnomAD version 3.1 to gather allele frequencies for local ancestry blocks identified in 7,612 Latino admixed individuals with varying proportions of European, Amerindigenous, and African ancestry', using gnomAD's pre-computed local ancestry calls; produces Figure 5C and the pairwise frequency-difference distributions.

headline.static_readiness: 0/19 (0%) - stage1 ceiling only, no R-star (R-star needs stage-2 code verification)
headline.inference_inclusive_upper_bound: NI on all 19 computational steps; RI is reached on none of them. The binding constraint is the version axis alone, and it binds absolutely: the paper's Methods name at least ten distinct pieces of software - FLARE, SeSAMe / openSeSAMe, methylClock, DunedinPACE, the impute R library, cocor, R's stats library, bedtools, UCSC liftOver, and R itself - and give a version number for none of them. Every software citation is a literature citation (Browning 2023, Zhou 2018, Pelegi-Siso 2021, Belsky 2022, Diedenhofen and Musch 2015, Quinlan and Hall 2010, Hinrichs 2006), not a version pin, so version = 0 on every step and every step drops to NI regardless of how well the other axes score. The other three axes are in fact respectable: the code repository (github.com/seba2550/methyl-clocks-admixture, HTTP 200, last pushed 2026-07-10) is live and public with eleven numbered R scripts explicitly mapped to manuscript figures, so code = 2 on twelve of the nineteen steps; the MAGENTA methylation series is public in GEO as GSE338167 (status 'Public on Jul 10, 2026'), so data = 2 on fourteen steps; and the parameter axis is 2 on twelve steps because the SeSAMe filtering thresholds, the FDR procedures, the regression covariates and the statistical tests are stated explicitly. The only version-like identifiers anywhere in the paper are resource versions rather than software versions (gnomAD v3.0, v3.1 and v4.1, Illumina HumanMethylation EPICv2.0, the 1000 Genomes CEU / PEL / YRI panels), which do not lift the version axis. The repository's environment.yml is a conda specification, not a lock: it declares 'python>=3.9' and 'r-base>=4.0' and then lists every remaining dependency by bare name with no constraint at all (pandas, numpy, scipy, scikit-learn, matplotlib, seaborn, r-tidyverse, r-patchwork, r-cowplot, r-ggpubr, r-gridextra, r-devtools, r-boot, r-readxl, r-quadprog, r-magick, bioconductor-geoquery, bioconductor-methylclock, bioconductor-biocmanager), and it omits several tools the Methods actually use (sesame, DunedinPACE, cocor, impute, bedtools, liftOver, FLARE). Solving that environment today would resolve to whatever conda-forge and bioconda currently serve, which is why the capture claim is recorded as floating and not as env_lock_claimed. A second, independent obstacle is version-of-record drift: the repository README describes the later eLife article (10.7554/eLife.105343.2) with replication cohorts (GENOA, Grady Trauma Project, Swedish), principal-component clocks and a renumbered six-figure layout that do not exist in the assessed bioRxiv v2 preprint, and the repository carries zero releases and zero tags, so there is no commit state corresponding to the preprint being assessed.
headline.coverage: 19 computational analysis steps assessed from the bioRxiv v2 full-text Methods subsections ('MAGENTA study Cohort Selection', 'Genetic data and ancestry analysis', 'Methylation profiles', 'Estimating epigenetic age and its correlation with chronological age in the MAGENTA study', 'Computing epigenetic age acceleration in Alzheimer's disease patients and controls', 'Evaluating ensembles of age predictors', 'Analysis of genetic variation at clock CpG sites', 'Analysis of meQTL affecting clock CpGs' including both its 'Identification of meQTL affecting clock CpGs' and 'Population-level allele frequencies of meQTL affecting clock CpGs' parts), plus the 'Data availability' and 'Code availability' statements, plus the landing page and README prose of github.com/seba2550/methyl-clocks-admixture and its environment.yml. 3 wet-lab / clinical steps (cohort ascertainment and blood collection, Global Screening Array genotyping, EPICv2.0 methylation array) counted in W and out of computational-reproduction scope. Coverage = 19/22 (86%) of enumerated steps. The differential-methylation section (Results 2.6) is described in the Methods only within the meQTL section's neighbourhood and was scored as C13 from the Results text, which carries the full parameterisation. Supplementary Figures 1-2 were not retrieved at stage 1.

gaps.missing: Not a single software version number appears anywhere in the paper. FLARE (C2), SeSAMe / openSeSAMe (C4), methylClock (C5, C7, C10), DunedinPACE (C6), the impute R library (C7), cocor (C9), R and its stats library (C11), bedtools (C14) and UCSC liftOver (C16) are each introduced by literature citation only. R itself is never versioned. Because methylClock bundles the clock coefficient sets and performs the age-acceleration decomposition, its version silently determines the numeric output of C5, C7, C10 and C12; because SeSAMe's openSeSAMe pipeline defines the probe-masking and Noob implementation, its version determines the beta matrix every downstream step consumes. Only external resources are versioned (gnomAD v3.0 / v3.1 / v4.1, Illumina EPICv2.0), and resource versions do not close the software axis.
gaps.how_to_close: Add a software table listing an exact version for every tool and every R / Bioconductor package used (R, sesame, methylclock, DunedinPACE, impute, cocor, bedtools, liftOver, FLARE), ideally generated from sessionInfo() captured at the time the published results were produced, and cite it from the Methods.

gaps.where: Whole analysis environment (all 19 computational steps); repository file environment.yml
gaps.missing: No environment lock is claimed in the paper at all - the Methods, Data availability and Code availability statements mention no container, no conda specification and no lockfile. The repository ships environment.yml, but it is a floating specification rather than a lock: two entries carry lower bounds only ('python>=3.9', 'r-base>=4.0') and the remaining nineteen entries are bare package names with no version constraint whatsoever. There is no conda-lock, no pixi.lock, no renv.lock, no requirements.txt with hashes, no Dockerfile and no image digest. Coverage is also partial: sesame, DunedinPACE, cocor, impute, bedtools, liftOver and FLARE do not appear in environment.yml even though the Methods use all seven, so the declared environment cannot execute the full pipeline as described.
gaps.how_to_close: Export a resolved conda-lock (or pixi.lock) for at least linux-64 from the environment that produced the results, add every missing dependency (sesame, DunedinPACE, cocor, impute, bedtools, ucsc-liftover, FLARE) to it, and cite the lockfile from the Code availability statement rather than the unconstrained environment.yml.

gaps.where: Entry point for C1, C2 and C3 - MAGENTA genotyping data; and the paper-stated entry point for C4 - MAGENTA methylation matrices
gaps.missing: The preprint's Data availability statement is forward-looking, not an accession: 'Raw and normalized beta matrices, along with genotyping data used in this study will be made available at time of publication in the NIAGADS platform.' No NIAGADS accession, dataset identifier or URL is given, and NIAGADS is a controlled-access repository requiring a data access request, so the genotype-dependent steps (genotype QC, FLARE local ancestry, global ancestry proportions) cannot be entered from anything the paper states. The repository partially supersedes this - it points to GEO GSE338167 for the MAGENTA methylation data (verified public, 'Public on Jul 10, 2026') and ships derived files data/genotyping_data/AA_ancestry_proportions.txt and HISPANIC_ancestry_proportions.txt - but the derived proportion files let a reader consume C3's output rather than reproduce C1-C3, and no accession for raw genotypes exists in either the paper or the repository.
gaps.how_to_close: Replace the 'will be made available' sentence with the actual GEO accession for the methylation data and the actual NIAGADS dataset identifier plus its access-request URL for the genotypes, and state explicitly which of the two routes (controlled genotypes versus shipped ancestry proportions) is intended as the reproduction entry point for the ancestry-stratified analyses.

gaps.where: External resources consumed at C2, C13, C14, C15, C16, C18, C19
gaps.missing: The 1000 Genomes CEU / PEL / YRI reference panels used by FLARE are named but no release, build or file identifier is given. The EWAS Hub whole-blood dataset supplying the 306 African-ancestry and 300 European-ancestry samples at C13 is named with no accession, no URL, no version and no sample manifest, so the differential-methylation result cannot be re-entered. The three meQTL summary-statistic sets (Hawe 2022, Shang 2023, Villicana 2023 / EPIGEN) are cited by publication only, with no accession or download URL and no download date; the repository README defers them to 'their respective repositories (such as the GENOA meQTL summary stats and SCREEN portals)', which is not a resolvable identifier either. The UCSC liftOver chain file used for the hg19 -> hg38 conversion at C16 is not named or dated. gnomAD is the one resource handled well - versions 3.0, 3.1 and 4.1 are each stated for the specific use they serve - but no download date or file checksum accompanies them.
gaps.how_to_close: Give an accession or a versioned download URL plus a download date for the EWAS Hub cohort, for each of the three meQTL summary-statistic sets and for the 1000 Genomes panels; name the liftOver chain file and its source; and record checksums for the gnomAD sites files actually consumed.

gaps.missing: Several invocations are named without the settings that determine their output. C1 states only 'standard quality control filters on call rate, quality, missingness, and Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium' with no thresholds. C2 gives FLARE's reference panels but no other arguments (genetic map, minimum MAF, model iterations). C6 says DunedinPACE was 'applied separately' with no invocation described. C7 names impute.knn but not k, the row/column maximum missingness or the random seed. C14 says the intersection 'was performed using bedtools' without the subcommand or any flags. C16 names liftOver with no chain file and no policy for records that fail to map. C18 reports p < 3.85e-25 for the African-versus-other-populations allele-frequency comparison without naming the test. The blanket sentence 'Unless otherwise specified, default options were used for all clocks' covers C5 but leaves the defaults dependent on the unstated methylClock version, so it does not close the parameter gap either.
gaps.how_to_close: Add a supplementary table of exact command lines and non-default arguments for FLARE, bedtools, liftOver and impute.knn; state the genotype QC thresholds numerically; name the statistical test behind every reported p-value; and pin the methylClock version so that 'default options' has a determinate meaning.

gaps.missing: The repository is live (HTTP 200, created 2024-08-17, last pushed 2026-07-10) but carries no persistent identifier: the GitHub API reports an empty releases list and an empty tags list, there is no Zenodo or Software Heritage DOI, and there is no LICENSE file, so redistribution and reuse rights for the analysis code are undeclared. Because there is no tag, the commit state that produced the assessed preprint cannot be recovered - and the current head does not correspond to the preprint at all (see gap type 9). The Code availability statement cites only the bare repository URL.
gaps.how_to_close: Cut a tagged release corresponding to each manuscript version, archive it in Zenodo with a DOI, cite the DOI (not the bare URL) in the Code availability statement, and add an OSI-approved LICENSE.

gaps.where: Derived intermediates underpinning C5-C12 and the figures
gaps.missing: The preprint promises 'Age predictions for all clocks mentioned in this article will be made available in tab-delimited format in the same Github repository in which all code used for these analyses is available.' The repository's declared data/ directory contains clock coefficient CSVs (Horvath_from_pkg.csv, Hannum_from_pkg.csv, EN_from_pkg.csv, PhenoAge_from_pkg.csv, DunedinPACE_from_pkg.csv), hg38 BED files of clock CpGs, and one file named bio_age_estimates_magenta_age_diff_metadata.csv - but no tab-delimited per-clock age prediction table is named in the README, and the normalised beta matrix (the actual input to every clock) is deferred to NIAGADS. The per-individual intrinsic and extrinsic age-acceleration values, the ensemble predictions, the differentially methylated CpG list from C13, and the 29,033-variant clock meQTL table from C17 are likewise not offered as released artifacts.
gaps.how_to_close: Publish, with checksums and a README inventory, the per-individual clock prediction and age-acceleration tables, the ensemble predictions, the differentially methylated CpG list and the clock meQTL variant table, so each figure can be regenerated from a stated intermediate even when the controlled-access inputs cannot be obtained.

gaps.where: Repository-versus-preprint correspondence; binding on every step for which code = 2 was credited (C5, C6, C8-C15, C17-C19)
gaps.missing: The repository README documents a different version of the study from the one assessed. It is titled 'Methylation Clocks Fail to Generalize Across Genetically Admixed Individuals' and cites eLife 10.7554/eLife.105343.2, and its eleven-script replication guide maps to figures that do not exist in the bioRxiv v2 preprint: it includes replication cohorts (GSE72680 Grady Trauma Project, GSE210254 GENOA, GSE87571 Swedish) that the preprint's Methods never mention, a principal-component clock analysis (scripts/10_pc_clocks.R) absent from the preprint, and a renumbered figure set in which the preprint's Figure 2 becomes Figures 2-4 and the preprint's Figures 4-6 collapse into a single Figure 6. Because there is no tag or release, no commit corresponding to the assessed preprint can be checked out. Code = 2 was therefore credited on the basis that a named script plausibly implements the preprint step, not on the basis that the script reproduces the preprint's reported numbers; a stage-2 assessment would have to establish that correspondence directly. Separately, the preprint's own Results section 2.6 (differential methylation between AFR and EUR individuals) carries its full parameterisation in Results rather than in Methods, and section 2.9 states '76% of its CpGs have an meQTL' where sections 2.7 and 2.9 elsewhere report 271/353 = 77%, a small internal inconsistency in the headline number.
gaps.how_to_close: Tag the repository at the commit that produced each manuscript version, state in the README which tag corresponds to which version (preprint v1, preprint v2, eLife), and reconcile the 76% / 77% Horvath meQTL figure in the text.
